classification.difficultyReason: Follow the supplied dissection, subtract side lengths and compare two expressions for the same area; the identity and rearrangement are explicitly scaffolded.

content.prompt:
The following leads you through the geometrical proof that $a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)$.

In the diagram opposite, square $ECFG$, of side length $b$, is cut out of square $ABCD$, which has side length $a$.

spec.description: Square ABCD with bottom-right square ECFG removed; dashed cut HG and right-angle cue at H. Ordinary source blue outlines are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: AB=AD=a; EC=CF=EG=GF=b; H, G and E are collinear. Coordinates encode a representative a>b, without introducing numerical dimensions.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry, vertex labels and supplied dimensions are permanent givens; no response values are printed.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the area of hexagon $ABEGFD$?

answer.worked:
Subtract the area of the removed square from the area of the original square.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }ABEGFD&=a\times a-b\times b\\\text{Area of }ABEGFD&=a^2-b^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: The rectangle $HGFD$ is moved so that $DF$ is placed on top of $BE$ (see diagram).

spec.description: Rearranged shaded rectangle, with original piece on the left and moved piece on the right. Coincident B,D and E,F labels retain the dissection correspondence. Light blue fill identifies the region named in d(i); ordinary outlines are black.
spec.mathematics: Adjacent top lengths a and b give total width a+b; height is a-b. The common vertical boundary represents coincident BE and DF.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied segment labels and shading remain visible; the product for the area is withheld.

children.label: i
children.prompt: What is the area of the large shaded rectangle?

answer.worked:
Rearranging the pieces preserves their total area. The original hexagon and the new rectangle therefore have equal areas:

$$a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b).$$
